speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have a history of gait and limb ataxia; to narrow this down, could you tell me if you've noticed any recent memory changes, confusion, or personality shifts? Additionally, do you have a family history of similar neurological symptoms or a known genetic disorder?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that description; the "drunk" appearance suggests significant cerebellar involvement. Given your history, have you experienced any episodes of double vision, slurred speech, or difficulty swallowing that might indicate brainstem compression? Also, did your symptoms start gradually over months or were there specific episodes of sudden worsening?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is a crucial piece of information; natalizumab is known to increase the risk of Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML). Do you have any history of vision loss, cognitive decline, or weakness in addition to your ataxia? REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with and without contrast.
